summary:
At tag v02.08.02.60, infill_combination combines only sparse infill (stInternal regions). Walls, internal solid infill, floating vertical shell and bridges are still printed every layer. For this part, 0.16 mm layers on a 0.4 mm nozzle, it always merges exactly 2 layers into one 0.32 mm pass, starting from the bottom: layers 1+2 print at layer 2, 3+4 at layer 4, and so on. The rule is "stop when height reaches nozzle diameter". It does not look at max_layer_height (0.28 in this profile; a FIXME in the code says so), and the option infill_combination_max_layer_height does not exist at this tag. The combined line has the same width (0.45) and the same XY pattern. Its height is 0.32, so it carries 0.1220 mm3/mm, and the 7.5 mm3/s cap drops its speed from 112.8 to 61.5 mm/s. The pattern stays the same because line spacing is computed from layer_height, not from the combined height. So the time saved comes from printing half as many short, acceleration-limited moves and half the in-infill travel, not from extruding faster.

The G-codes show that sparse infill time is dominated by acceleration, not by the 7.5 mm3/s cap:
- 19,624 moves, median 1.15 mm, 82% shorter than 2 mm, 74% arcs.
- 95% of extrusion time is spent in moves that never reach cruise speed.
- Measured as production (no cooling slowdown, acceleration 6000): extrusion takes 393 s, against 226 s of pure cruise and a 222 s volumetric floor. Travel, wipe and retract inside the infill block add 69 s, for 462 s per piece in total.

This contradicts the context: "10m35s without cooling slowdown" overstates production sparse infill time. The Arachne single-piece file uses consistent_surface and prints sparse infill at 20–60 mm/s on most layers. The analyzer's de-slowdown model was written for uniform_cooling, so it does not remove that slowdown. The classic original (uniform_cooling) gives 403 s extrusion at acceleration 6000, which matches.

Simulated savings per piece in production:
- infill_combination: about −150 to −182 s (33–39% of sparse block time). Slope-induced slivers are negligible (0.05% of length). About 5–7% of sparse length sits next to solid infill in the paired layer and stays single-height.
- 12% density: about −65 to −80 s (14–17%).
- 10% density: about −100 to −130 s (22–28%).
- Combination + 12%: about −190 to −222 s (41–48%, about 3.2–3.7 min per piece, about 13–15 min per 4-piece plate).
- Combination + 10%: only about 20 s more per piece than combination + 12%.

Gyroid path length is not linear in density for this part. The crossing lines scale about linearly (80% at 12%, 70% at 10%, synthetic port of the code). The roughly 22–27% of length that follows the walls (line-to-line connections along the wall, kept while under 20 mm) stays roughly constant.

Recommendation: infill_combination = 1 and sparse_infill_density = 12% for the 4-piece production project. Do not use 10%.

claims.claim: Because of the rounded-bead flow model, one 0.32 combined line holds 1.835x, not 2x, the volume of a 0.16 line. Combination alone therefore cuts sparse infill volume by about 8% (about 1664 to about 1526 mm3) at the same density.
claims.evidence: Flow.cpp:219 formula: 0.32*(0.45-0.32*0.2146)=0.1220 vs 0.16*(0.45-0.16*0.2146)=0.0665 mm3/mm; research_c/sparse_analysis.py output combination_flow {mm3_per_mm_0.16: 0.06651, mm3_per_mm_0.32: 0.12202}.

claims.claim: No interaction with gyroid-specific options: infill_lock_depth, skin and skeleton apply only to the locked-zag pattern, and shift/rotate only to crosszag/zigzag. Gyroid takes its phase from print_z (the top layer of the pair), and the clearance used for gyroid is 0.5 x solid width.

claims.claim: On sloped walls combination can leave narrow per-layer slivers, and Fill grows collapsed narrow areas into the voids as extra solid infill. Measured for this part, the outer walls next to sparse infill are near-vertical: only about 13 mm (0.05%) of sparse length would become slope slivers. About 1.8 km (7%) of sparse length lies within 0.45 mm of solid infill in the paired layer and would stay single-height.

recommendation:
Apply these edits to the 4-piece production project only: variantes/Jogos_Vorazes_producao_4pecas.3mf, file Metadata/project_settings.config, through the variant generator:

"infill_combination": "1"
"sparse_infill_density": "12%"

Add both keys to the first entry of "different_settings_to_system", in alphabetical order, so the GUI shows them as modified:
"default_acceleration;enable_support;infill_combination;seam_position;sparse_infill_density;wall_generator"

Leave "sparse_infill_pattern": "gyroid" and everything else unchanged.

**Why combination.** It is the largest and safest lever for this part:
- It only regroups sparse infill. Walls, floating vertical shell, internal solid and bridges stay at 0.16 every layer. Internal bridges are planned before combination.
- About 93% of the sparse infill area is combinable, because the infill sits in near-vertical sections of the ring.
- It removes about 2.5–3.0 min per piece by halving the number of short, acceleration-limited moves.

**Why 12% and not 10%.**
- With combination already on, going from 12% to 10% only saves about 20 more seconds per piece (about 0.3 min, roughly 1.3 min per plate).
- The cost is a 5.35 mm gyroid pitch instead of 4.46 mm, with infill steps already 0.32 mm tall.
- Total infill material would drop by about 39% instead of about 27%: density × 0.917 flow factor, plus the roughly constant wall-following part.
- internal_bridge_support_thickness does nothing at this tag, so there is no mitigation for longer spans under internal solid, floating shell and the few top surfaces.

**Single-piece variant.** For now apply only "sparse_infill_density": "12%". Enable "infill_combination": "1" there only after slicing, and only if analisar_gcode.py shows no more outer-wall layers below 60 mm/s than today (71). In a single piece, combination leaves every other layer with no sparse infill to slow down, so under consistent_surface the outer wall gets slowed instead. On silk that means alternating gloss.

**Interaction with the third Etapa C candidate.** If ensure_vertical_shell_thickness is set to partial, solid shell area turns into sparse infill. That area will then also be combined and thinned, so evaluate those regions together on the same test print.
expected_time_effect:
All figures are per piece, estimated from the planner on the existing G-code. They assume production conditions: acceleration 6000, no cooling slowdown (the 4-piece plate has every layer above 8 s except one).

**Baseline.** The sparse infill block takes about 462 s (7.7 min): 393 s of extrusion plus 69 s of travel, wipe and retract inside the block. It is not 10m35s: that figure includes the single-piece file's consistent_surface slowdown.

| Option | Saved per piece | Share of sparse infill time |
|---|---|---|
| infill_combination = 1 | −150 to −182 s (−2.5 to −3.0 min) | 33–39% |
| 12% density | −65 to −80 s (−1.1 to −1.3 min) | 14–17% |
| 10% density | −100 to −130 s (−1.7 to −2.2 min) | 22–28% |
| Combination + 12% | about −190 to −222 s (−3.2 to −3.7 min) | about 41–48% |
| Combination + 10% | about −205 to −240 s (−3.4 to −4.0 min) | about 45–52% |

- **Combination.** Simulated upper bound 182 s; the classic original gives 188 s. About 7% of sparse infill stays single-height next to solid regions, and Fill may add small solid pieces.
- **12% / 10% alone.** The crossing lines scale with density, but about 22–27% of the length (the part that follows the walls) does not shrink.
- **Combination + 12% / 10%.** On top of combination, 12% adds about −40 s and 10% about −58 s.
- **Whole plate.** Combination + 12% is about −13 to −15 min per 4-piece plate, about 5–6% of per-piece print time.

**What only slicing can tell:**
- the real intersection and leftover geometry;
- the extra solid pieces Fill adds next to the removed infill;
- how many gyroid lines survive in narrow islands at 12%;
- Bambu's own time estimate.

**Single piece.** The gain is smaller (crude estimate about −135 s with combination) and it needs the outer-wall check described above.
visual_risks: Combination prints infill as a 0.32 mm bead, above the profile's max_layer_height of 0.28; the combine logic ignores that limit. Every other layer, a bead with twice the volume touches the inner wall (infill_wall_overlap 15%). On a 2-wall silk shell this could show as a faint every-other-layer texture or infill pattern through the surface. This is plausible but unproven, and only a print will tell.

Single-piece prints only: with combination, every other layer loses its sparse infill, which is the time consistent_surface slows down first. The outer wall would then be slowed on those layers, giving alternating gloss bands on silk. The 4-piece plate is not affected.

Lower density increases the unsupported spans under internal bridges, internal solid and the floating vertical shell: 3.57 mm at 15%, 4.46 mm at 12%, 5.35 mm at 10%. Possible effects are pinholes or pillowing on the small top surfaces and on gently upward-sloping areas near the top of the ring (z 56–64), and sag under shells next to the walls. internal_bridge_support_thickness does nothing at this tag, so there is no mitigation.

Combination plus lower density reduces stiffness behind the thin shell: about 27% less infill material at 12% (about 39% at 10%). Most of the infill is in z 24–48 mm (up to 121 mm of infill per layer at 32–40 mm). A softer backing there could let the shell flex or show where infill touches it.

Next to solid regions, combination leaves narrow single-height leftovers and adds small solid infill pieces (Fill.cpp:386-459). These are internal and not visible, but they create extra short segments and seams inside the shell.
what_to_check_after_slicing: CONFIG_BLOCK contains "; infill_combination = 1" and "; sparse_infill_density = 12%"; "; sparse_infill_pattern = gyroid" and "; wall_generator = arachne" are unchanged.

Sparse infill appears with full length only on every second layer: Z_HEIGHT 0.52, 0.84, 1.16, ..., i.e. z = 0.2 + 0.16·2k. Today 379 layers have "; FEATURE: Sparse infill". Expect about 190 layers with normal-length blocks; the other layers should have only short leftover blocks (total about ≤7% of today's 25.5 m).

Inside the combined blocks the feed is about F3688 (61.5 mm/s), not F6766.287. E per mm is about 0.0497 (0.1220 mm3/mm × 0.98 / 2.405), against 0.0271 today. LINE_WIDTH is still 0.45 and "; LAYER_HEIGHT:" is still 0.16 on every layer.

Run analisar_gcode.py. Sparse infill length should drop from 25.5 m to about 11–12 m (combination + 12%) and volume from about 1664 to about 1200–1250 mm3. Outer wall, Inner wall, Floating vertical shell (10.5 m / 697 mm3), Internal solid infill (4.9 m / 309 mm3), Bridge and Top surface should change by no more than a few percent. A new or larger 'Internal solid infill' at layers next to removed infill would be the extra solid pieces.

Run research_c/sparse_analysis.py on the new G-code. Sparse block time at acceleration 6000, nominal should be about 240–280 s, against 462 s today. The Bambu estimate for the 4-piece plate should drop by about 13–15 min against the Etapa B projection.

Single-piece variant only, if combination is enabled there: compare the analisar_gcode outer-wall speed table by height band. There should be no more than 71 layers with the outer wall below 60 mm/s, and no alternating pattern.

Physical, 4-piece test plate: single light at 45°, part turned to 4 positions. Look for faint every-other-layer texture or infill pattern showing through, especially at z 24–48 mm where the infill is densest. Compare with the reference part.

Physical: loupe on the top surfaces and gentle upward slopes near the top of the ring (z 56–64 mm), looking for pinholes or pillowing. Press the shell lightly with a finger to compare stiffness against the reference part.
Physical: weigh the parts. Expect about 0.5 g less PLA per piece (about 0.44 cm3 less infill) with combination + 12%. A larger drop would point to under-extrusion of the 0.32 mm infill.
